title: Conversational slab concentrator with KV proactive thresholding
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design and implement a session-level slab concentrator that groups concurrent streaming chat turns from heterogeneous sessions to maximize GPU utilization while proactively controlling KV cache inflation. The feature should reduce P95 latency regressions under high-concurrency tails and limit peak GPU memory to avoid OOMs without sacrificing throughput. This ticket covers algorithm design, simulator validation, a small-run canary in Dedicated, and integration with the existing KV cache compaction/TTL pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator shows >=12% reduction in peak GPU memory usage on SLAB workload compared to baseline microbatcher at identical throughput
End-to-end P95 latency remains within 10% of baseline for low-latency sessions while P50 improves by >=5% under medium load
KV cache growth rate limited to <1.5x baseline at 95th percentile concurrent sessions
Canary in dedicated cluster runs for 24 hours with no OOMs and no customer-facing errors
Code merged and feature gated behind runtime-1.22 flag; design doc and runbook published
tasks: Write slab concentrator prototype that creates 'fusion groups' based on session affinity and token-turn density
Add proactive KV thresholding: prefetch window heuristics + spill-to-host policy for low-priority groups
Build a synthetic workload simulator (fifo+bursty chat patterns) and compare against baseline packer
Integrate with GPU allocator to reserve soft-slices and enforce group-level memory budgets
Create observability hooks: per-group token-rate, kv-resident-size, soft-reserve-violations
Canary deploy on dedicated-qa, run 24h soak, gather metrics and error traces
Document rollout plan, revert criteria, and troubleshooting runbook
comments: 2026-03-01 - Avery Chen: Initial triage. Observed recurring GPU memory spikes in streaming chat e2e tests when many long context sessions are open concurrently. Creating focused heuristic to trade slight batching for bounded memory.

2026-03-03 - Rajat Patel: Proto algorithm: form 'fusion groups' by hashing session intent fingerprint + recent token density; allow heterogeneous session lengths with max-group-resident-kv threshold. Opened draft design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Conversational+Slab+Concentrator

2026-03-05 - Maya Thompson (review): Concern about fairness — lower-priority sessions may see latency increase. Recommendation: implement per-session latency SLO token budget and a decay-based re-prioritization every 50ms.

2026-03-07 - Rajat Patel: Implemented simulator and ran 3k-run sweep. Results: peak GPU mem reduced 14% on average; KV-resident-size 1.4x baseline at heavy tail (meets threshold); but 2% P95 latency regression for <50-token sessions. Added 'fast-path' bypass for sessions under 32 tokens.
2026-03-09 - EngInfra: Allocator integration notes - need API to reserve soft-slices per group. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2481

2026-03-11 - SRE: Canary plan approved. Metrics to monitor: p50/p95 latency by session-length, kv-resident-bytes, soft-reserve-violations, OOM count. Grafana dash: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streaming/conv-slab-concentrator

2026-03-13 - Rajat Patel: Canary started on dedicated-qa. Early telemetry: group consolidation reduced per-GPU kernel launch overheads (improved throughput) and spike frequency dropped. Noted two soft-reserve violations after long-running low-priority bursts — tuning spill-to-host threshold next.
2026-03-14 - Avery Chen: Product requested summary for PM sync. Preparing short write-up and rollout checklist. Planning a design review on 2026-03-18.
